requirement:
`languages::name_for_path` returns the name that the SDK's filename-based
constructors would select under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
The lookup uses only the path and works for files that do not exist.

```rust,ignore
pub fn name_for_path(path: &Path) -> &'static str;
```
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.name_for_path` is the prescribed signature `pub fn name_for_path(path: &Path) -> &'static str;`. An alternative with a different signature, such as taking `impl AsRef<Path>` or returning `String`, could produce the same runtime results but would not match the text. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs#fn[name_for_path]` is marked {impl} and declares exactly `pub fn name_for_path(path: &std::path::Path) -> &'static str`. That covers the signature obligation.

The other clauses describe behavior: the function returns the name the filename-based constructors would select, it uses only the path, and it works for files that do not exist. I treated them as observable behavior rather than structure. The text does not require delegation to a particular interface. The function does delegate to `profile_for_path` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/profile.rs`, which looks the path up in the language registry. That lookup uses only the path, so it fits these clauses. Tests can check that behavior.

`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults` is cited for context only, so it adds no structural obligation here.

behavioral: Obligations in `requirements.sdk.outlines.name_for_path`: (1) `languages::name_for_path` returns the name the filename-based constructors would select under `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`. (2) The lookup uses only the path. (3) It works for files that do not exist. The signature is a structural choice, so it is not a behavioral obligation here.

The test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[default_language_names_match_the_retained_outline]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It builds paths in a temp dir and never creates the files, so it covers (3) and, in practice, (2). The cases are `LIB.RS` (rust), `widget.TSX` (tsx), `README` (plain-text) and `foo.unknown` (plain-text). They cover an uppercase extension, a no-extension name and an unknown extension. For each case it asserts `languages::name_for_path(&path) == name`. It also builds `OutlineContent::from_source` on the same path and asserts `root.language() == name`. That ties the function to the constructors' selection, which is obligation (1).

The test does not name Python, TypeScript, Markdown, CSS, TOML or YAML. I read `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs#fn[name_for_path]`. It only returns `profile_for_path(path).name`, with no mapping or branching of its own. The per-language mappings belong to `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults` and the language chapters, which are assessed separately. I found no plausible way for `name_for_path` to violate its text that this test would accept.
